We need a CloudFormation template that creates Glue catalog databases and tables for querying a Neptune graph dataset via Athena, supporting both property graph and RDF models using the Neptune Athena connector. The airport, country, and continent tables should each be configured as a vertex-type table with a graph label matching their own table name (airport, country, and continent respectively). The route table should be configured as an edge-type table with a graph label of route. The customairport table should be configured as a view-type table. The customairport view uses the following exact Gremlin traversal query to select source and destination airport codes for up to 10 routes: "g.V().hasLabel(\"airport\").as(\"source\").out(\"route\").as(\"destination\").select(\"source\",\"destination\").by(\"code\").limit(10)". For the RDF database, include a table named airport_rdf with the same column structure as the LPG airport table, plus a classuri parameter set to "class:Airport", a prefix_class parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/class/, a prefix_prop parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/datatypeProperty/, a querymode of class, and this table should be marked as an rdf-type table with a subject setting of id, a predicate prefix setting of prop, and stripping of URI prefixes enabled (strip_uri true). Also include two route tables named route_rdf and route_rdf_nopfx, both with incode, outcode, and dist columns, a querymode of sparql, marked as rdf-type tables with stripping of URI prefixes enabled (strip_uri true). The route_rdf table uses a prefix_prop parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/datatypeProperty/ and a prefix_op parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/objectProperty/, with the following exact SPARQL query text for selecting route codes and distances: "select ?incode ?outcode ?dist where { ?resin op:route ?resout . GRAPH ?route { ?resin op:route ?resout } . ?route prop:dist ?dist . ?resin prop:code ?incode . ?resout prop:code ?outcode . }". The route_rdf_nopfx table uses the same prefix_prop and prefix_op parameters but embeds the prefix declarations directly inside the query text instead of relying on the separate parameters, using this exact query: "PREFIX prop: <http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/datatypeProperty/> PREFIX op: <http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/objectProperty/> select ?incode ?outcode ?dist where { ?resin op:route ?resout . GRAPH ?route { ?resin op:route ?resout } . ?route prop:dist ?dist . ?resin prop:code ?incode . ?resout prop:code ?outcode . }".

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an automated photo analysis system. Users will upload images to an S3 bucket, and the system will use Amazon Rekognition to detect whether the image contains a human. The state machine invokes a Rekognition Lambda to analyze the image, then either notifies via another Lambda that publishes to SNS or passes through if no human is detected. The template must handle the circular dependency between the S3 bucket's event notification configuration and the Lambda permission, ensuring the bucket can trigger the initial Lambda. Output the bucket name for uploading.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates custom SSM automation documents to enable VPC Flow Logs across all VPCs, including a Change Manager integration that invokes the primary automation via a change request execution. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive set of CloudWatch alarms for monitoring a fixed set of EC2 instances: i-01fcfb64dffcc4b37, i-02b6521ddb3bff251, i-060735a613a30fe52, i-0db9db4ebf6de21f4, and i-0f63a59d448a0cdbe. We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Elemental MediaPackage channel with HLS and DASH origin endpoints for live streaming, and optionally sets up VOD workflows using an S3 bucket for source content and an archive bucket for live-to-VOD, with the ability to specify the output type (defaulting to APPLE_HLS, with ISO_DASH and ALL also supported), manifest name (defaulting to index), segment duration in seconds (defaulting to 3), and startover window in seconds (defaulting to 0), using a logical name prefix for resource naming (defaulting to MediaPackage) and tagging with an environment tag (defaulting to production) and a custom key-value tag (defaulting to createdby and aws-cloudformation-templates).

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC endpoint for a specified AWS service (CloudWatch, ECR, S3, or SES) within an existing VPC infrastructure for testing private connectivity, accepting two parameters: Environment (with allowed values prod and staging, default staging) and EndpointService (with allowed values cloudwatch, ecr, s3, ses, default s3), and conditionally deploys the correct VPC endpoint type (a Gateway endpoint for S3 and Interface endpoints for the other services), imports the VPC ID, subnet IDs for interface endpoints, route table IDs for the Gateway endpoint, and the VPC CIDR from a parent stack named bashlinux-<Environment>, and creates a dedicated security group for interface endpoints that allows HTTPS traffic from the VPC CIDR, with an additional security group for SES allowing SMTP ports 465 and 587.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an SQS queue for audit events with a dead letter queue only in non-development environments, using a KMS customer-managed key with automatic rotation and an alias, where the main queue has a message retention of 1 hour in dev and 14 days otherwise, a visibility timeout of 30 seconds in dev and 70 otherwise, a receive message wait time of 20 seconds, a redrive policy that denies all redrives and sends failed messages to the DLQ after 10 receives in non-dev, and queue policies (applied to the main queue only in non-dev environments, since the TxMA account mapping has no entry for dev) that allow the TxMA account (mapped per environment) to read, delete, and get attributes, and allow EventBridge to send messages; the DLQ should also allow EventBridge to send messages; the KMS key policy must grant full access to the account root, and in non-dev allow the TxMA account to decrypt and EventBridge to decrypt and generate data keys; an IAM role with a Lambda trust policy and basic execution permissions (logs) should be created only in non-dev, optionally bound by a permissions boundary parameter; two CloudWatch alarms should be created only in non-dev-like environments, one on the main queue's ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage with a threshold of 86400 seconds and one on the DLQ's ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible using a max-min expression with a threshold of 1, both sending OK and alarm actions to an imported SNS topic from a provided BuildNotificationStackName; the template should accept parameters for environment (dev, build, staging, integration, production), a permissions boundary ARN (default empty), a support manual URL, a service name, and the build notification stack name, and export the queue name, URL, ARN, encryption key ARN, and conditionally the DLQ ARN.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS WAF Regional WebACL for protecting a regional resource, such as an ALB or API Gateway, against common web attacks; the WebACL should have a default action of ALLOW and include a rule to block manually specified IP addresses (using an initially empty IP set that can be populated later), a rule that counts requests with a body larger than 8192 bytes (for detection and monitoring), a rule to block SQL injection attacks by inspecting the query string and body with both URL decode and HTML entity decode transformations plus the URI with URL decode transformation only, and a rule to block cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks using the same field-to-match and transformation approach, and the template must accept a single parameter for the WebACL name with a default value of "CommonAttackProtection" that prefixes all resource and metric names.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Kafka application stack for testing purposes in the ap-southeast-2 region, using nested templates stored in a build bucket (dchash2buildbucket) for the security group, IAM role, and EC2 instance definitions, and it must deploy three standalone EC2 instances (one per Availability Zone) into private subnets imported from an existing VPC stack named UAT-VPC, attach an IAM instance profile referencing a managed policy imported from a stack named IAM-ManagedPolicy-EC2Instances, use the AMI ami-XXXXXXXX and the key pair DCHash2-TestKey, default to a t2.micro instance type, and apply tagging with Environment=UAT, BusinessUnit=Gaming, Department=BrandName, Application=SomePlatform, and Component=Kafka.

The template should define five saved queries: one that filters for recent error messages matching the pattern "ERROR" and sorts them by timestamp descending, one that analyzes Lambda REPORT log entries to compute average and percentile (50th, 95th, 99th) durations grouped in 5-minute bins, one that parses log messages for a "level" field and counts occurrences by level, one that parses messages for "route" and "latency_ms" fields to calculate average, maximum, and 95th percentile latency per route, and one that filters for entries containing an "@initDuration" field to identify cold starts sorted by duration. All queries should be named with a "dva-lab-09-02/" prefix and target the specified log group.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a serverless Maths MCP (Model Context Protocol) server with API Gateway, Lambda, and Cognito authentication for testing purposes. The Cognito user pool should enforce password policies (minimum 8 characters, uppercase, lowercase, numbers), allow email auto-verification, and use email as username. The app client should allow password-based auth flows with 1-hour access/id token validity and 30-day refresh token validity. Use default parameter values: DeploymentStage = 'dev', UserPoolName = 'maths-mcp-users', AppClientName = 'maths-mcp-client'. The API should be regional, and the Lambda function should have a placeholder handler that will be updated later. Do not include any additional resources beyond what is necessary for this core setup.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a cost management stack to monitor and manage AWS costs, including a monthly budget with a configurable limit defaulting to $100 USD, and notifications sent via SMS or email when actual costs exceed 80% and 99% of the budget, with the notification method and endpoint parameterized (defaulting to SMS with country code +61), and using a KMS key with alias "billing-topic-key" to encrypt the SNS topic, while following standard security and operational best practices.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a comprehensive monitoring and data extraction pipeline for an internal QuickSight admin console, using multiple Glue jobs (both Python shell and ETL) to periodically collect metadata, asset access details, folder structures, dataset properties, data source properties, and Q topics information, storing all output in a private S3 bucket named admin-suite- followed by the account ID, with the Glue scripts located under s3://admin-console-cfn-dataprepare-code/glue/scripts/2025/ and the jobs scheduled to run every 3 hours via Glue triggers, along with CloudWatch metric streams covering key QuickSight metrics for ingestion, dashboard views, SPICE capacity, Q index, and Q action counts, each feeding into a dedicated Kinesis Firehose delivery stream that writes to the same S3 bucket with appropriate prefixes, and all of this managed by a single IAM role with permissions for QuickSight, Glue, S3, CloudWatch, Firehose, and IAM operations.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates three CloudWatch alarms for testing how different TreatMissingData settings affect alarm state transitions, all monitoring the same "AlwaysOK" metric from the AWS/NetworkELB namespace with a threshold of 100, a comparison operator of greater-than-or-equal-to-threshold, one evaluation period, a period of 60 seconds, and Minimum statistic; the three alarms should be named AlwaysOKAlarm, AlwaysFAILAlarm, and AlwaysINSUFFICIENTAlarm, with their TreatMissingData properties set to "notBreaching", "breaching", and "missing" respectively, and all alarms must have actions disabled.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the MongoDB backend service for a Docker-based voting application, running on AWS Fargate with an internal Network Load Balancer for TCP traffic on port 27017, using the default mongo image and a container port of 27017, with CPU set to 1024 and memory to 2048, and a desired count of 1; the template should import the VPC, public subnets, Fargate container security group, ECS cluster name, and ECS task execution role from an existing environment stack identified by a parameter named EnvironmentName (defaulting to "voteapp"), and it must output the MongoDB URI as the load balancer DNS name with port 27017.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Docker-based voting API service on ECS Fargate, integrated with an existing Application Load Balancer and ECS cluster, for a multi-service environment. The template should define a task definition using a provided Docker image URL, set up a target group with health checks and stickiness, attach a listener rule to route traffic to the service based on a path pattern, and configure auto-scaling with step scaling policies triggered by CloudWatch CPU alarms. The service must run in public subnets with public IPs enabled, use a Fargate container security group, and reference an existing VPC, cluster, ALB listener, and Redis endpoint via stack exports. Key parameters include environment name (default "voteapp"), service name (default "voteapi"), image URL, container port (default 3000), CPU (default 1024) and memory (default 2048), desired count (default 2), path (default "*"), listener rule priority (default 1), and an optional IAM role and Mongo URI. The template should also create a CloudWatch log group for container logs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the foundational infrastructure for an ML workshop, leveraging AWS Service Catalog products to provision S3 buckets with KMS keys and IAM roles (version v2.1) and a VPC with private subnets across two Availability Zones, then storing all resultant resource references as SSM parameters under a common suffix. The VPC should use a CIDR of 10.229.0.0/16, private subnets in us-east-2a and us-east-2b with CIDRs 10.229.30.0/24 and 10.229.40.0/24 respectively, and VPC flow logs enabled. The template must accept parameters for the AZ names, CIDRs, flow logs toggle, and a suffix string (default "reinforce15") to uniquely name resources and parameter paths. It should create SSM parameters for the subnet IDs, IAM roles (SageMakerRole, NotebookInstanceRole, GetNewRevisionRole), S3 bucket names (data and infra), KMS key IDs (data capture and ML storage), and security groups that come from the Service Catalog products.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with a public and a private subnet, where the private subnet instances can access the internet through a NAT gateway placed in the public subnet. The VPC CIDR should default to 172.18.0.0/16, the public subnet to 172.18.0.0/22, and the private subnet to 172.18.32.0/21. The template should include an internet gateway, appropriate route tables and associations, and a NAT gateway with an Elastic IP attached to it. The public subnet should have auto-assign public IP enabled, while the private subnet should not. This is for testing outbound connectivity from private resources.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates three private subnets in the us-east-1 region spread across availability zones a, b, and c, each with a dedicated route table and an associated default route pointing to the respective NAT gateway exported from an existing public subnet stack that follows the naming convention of region-synapse-dev-vpc-2-public-subnets, along with subnet-to-NACL associations using the default NACL from the existing VPC stack named region-synapse-dev-vpc-2, and an S3 VPC endpoint attached to the private route tables to allow private access to S3; the subnets must use the CIDRs 10.24.24.0/24, 10.24.25.0/24, and 10.24.26.0/24 respectively, with MapPublicIpOnLaunch set to false, and the stack should export a comma-separated list of private subnet IDs, route table IDs, and the subnet group CIDR 10.24.24.0/21, using the stack name and region in the export names.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates composite CloudWatch alarms for monitoring the health of a cross-region failover application, specifically targeting the Remittance API in API Gateway, the GetRemittances and CreateRemittance Lambda functions, and the dbcluster1-instance1 RDS instance, with composite alarms named API Gateway Health, Lambda Health, and RDS Health that each aggregate their underlying metric alarms with an OR-based alarm rule so that any single triggered condition trips the composite. For the API Gateway Remittance API, alarm on 4XX errors averaging above 0 over a 300 second period, 5XX errors averaging above 1 over a 60 second period, and latency at or above 10000 milliseconds over a 300 second period, each evaluated over a single evaluation period with one datapoint to alarm and TreatMissingData explicitly set to notBreaching. For the GetRemittances and CreateRemittance Lambda functions, alarm when summed errors exceed 0 over a 60 second period and when summed invocations exceed 2 over a 60 second period, each with a single evaluation period, one datapoint to alarm, and TreatMissingData explicitly set to notBreaching (the invocations alarms should feed into the Lambda Health composite as well, though note the composite alarm rule itself only needs to reference the errors and duration alarms), while the two Duration alarms (average duration at or above 10000 milliseconds over a 900 second period, with a single evaluation period and one datapoint to alarm) are configured differently, with TreatMissingData explicitly set to missing (CloudWatch's standard default treatment) rather than notBreaching. For the dbcluster1-instance1 RDS instance, alarm on high CPU utilization averaging at or above 70 percent, a database connection count averaging at or above 100, deadlocks averaging at or above 10, network transmit and receive throughput each averaging at or above 10485760 bytes, a query count averaging at or above 100, a disk queue depth averaging at or above 50, and read and write latency each averaging at or above 0.1 seconds, each evaluated over a 300 second period with a single evaluation period and one datapoint to alarm, leaving TreatMissingData unset on every RDS alarm so CloudWatch's standard default missing-data treatment applies rather than explicitly notBreaching.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito-based authentication layer for a Lex chatbot web UI, supporting both authenticated and unauthenticated access, with IAM roles for either Lex V1 or Lex V2 depending on which bot is provided, and an optional policy to allow invoking a live chat API. The template should include a Cognito user pool with email as the username alias and auto-verified email, requiring given_name, family_name, email, and preferred_username as required attributes, a user pool client with no secret, and a Cognito identity pool that allows unauthenticated identities and is linked to the user pool. It must also create identity pool role attachments and separate IAM roles for authenticated and unauthenticated users, each with appropriate trust policies for Cognito and policies that grant either Lex V1 actions (like PostText and PostContent) or Lex V2 actions (like RecognizeText and RecognizeUtterance) based on a condition, plus a Polly synthesise speech permission for authenticated roles. The template should accept parameters for the identity pool name (default "identity pool"), the Lex V1 bot name (default "OrderFlowers") and optional Lex V2 bot ID and alias ID, a ForceCognitoLogin flag (default false) that, when true, denies unauthenticated Lex and API actions, and a ShouldEnableLiveChat flag (default false) that conditionally adds an execute-api invoke permission for a livechat endpoint. The deployment should choose Lex V1 if the bot name is provided and Lex V2 if the bot ID is provided, and the template should export the identity pool ID, user pool ID, and user pool client ID as outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS IoT policy and an IoT thing for testing Amazon FreeRTOS connectivity, with the policy named "FreeRTOSIoTPolicy" allowing Connect, Publish, Subscribe, and Receive actions for all resources, and a thing named "MyFreeRTOSThing" with a simple attribute key-value pair.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS cluster with the Fargate launch type for testing purposes, using an EnvironmentName parameter that defaults to "ecs-course" for namespacing all resources. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Redis service named redis-lead running in ECS Fargate for an environment named chat, using the latest Redis image listening on port 6379, with 512 CPU and 1024 MB of memory, routing all traffic from the public load balancer via a default path priority of 1, running a single task, and storing container logs in a dedicated log group named after the environment and service name.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a SageMaker Data Quality Job Definition for monitoring the model endpoint named my-endpoint, using a custom Docker image from ECR, an IAM role that SageMaker can assume, and a specific KMS key for encryption, writing its monitoring output to the S3 location s3://my-sagemaker-bucket/output, with the job running on a single ml.m5.xlarge instance and a 20GB volume, and stopping after one hour.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the authenticated and unauthenticated IAM roles for an AWS Amplify auth sandbox backend, each trusting an existing Cognito identity pool with ID us-east-1:b05b7842-b63f-40a6-8832-946b23db5909 via web identity federation, tagged with Amplify sandbox metadata. The template does not create a Cognito user pool, app client, or identity pool itself.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16, two public subnets (10.0.1.0/24 and 10.0.2.0/24) and two private subnets (10.0.11.0/24 and 10.0.12.0/24) spread across two Availability Zones, along with an Internet Gateway, a public route table with a default route to the Internet, two NAT Gateways (one per AZ) each with an Elastic IP and associated private route tables for outbound traffic from the private subnets, VPC Flow Logs that log all traffic to a CloudWatch Log Group with a configurable retention period (default 14 days) and traffic type (default ALL), and three VPC Endpoints: a Gateway endpoint for S3 (added to all route tables) and Interface endpoints for ECR API and ECR DKR placed in the private subnets with private DNS enabled; the template should be region-agnostic and include a mapping for AZ letters per region.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Fault Injection Simulator (FIS) experiment template designed for chaos engineering testing across multiple AWS services, which will block application network traffic from an experiment region to a target region of us-west-2 and pause cross-region replication for a configurable duration of PT20M, targeting resources tagged with ChaosAllowed set to true specifically for transit gateways, subnets, S3 buckets, and DynamoDB global tables, along with the necessary IAM roles and policies to allow FIS to perform actions like disrupting transit gateway and subnet connectivity, pausing S3 bucket replication, and pausing DynamoDB Global Table replication, and including a CloudWatch log group encrypted with a KMS key for experiment logging.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a networking foundation for an MWAA BPG Spark Pipeline infrastructure, including a VPC with a CIDR of 10.192.0.0/16, two public subnets (10.192.10.0/24 and 10.192.11.0/24) and two private subnets (10.192.20.0/24 and 10.192.21.0/24) spread across two availability zones, with the public subnets tagged for Kubernetes load balancer use and the private subnets tagged for internal load balancer use, along with NAT gateways in each public subnet to provide outbound internet access for the private subnets, and the whole stack should be prefixed with the project name "MWAA-BPG-Spark-Pipeline" for all resource naming, and we also need VPC flow logs enabled with a 30-day retention period and encrypted using a customer-managed KMS key with rotation enabled.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a few parameters in the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and a secret in Secrets Manager with a dynamically generated password, along with a Lambda function that retrieves and prints all parameters under the stack's path and all secrets matching that prefix, demonstrating how to use the SSM and Secrets Manager APIs; the Lambda should be named ParameterStoreDemo, use Python 3.12, read the stack name from an environment variable, and include the necessary IAM role and permissions to access the parameters and secrets.
We need a CloudFormation template that creates an HTTP API Gateway named "child" with a GET /orders endpoint defined inline via OpenAPI for testing purposes.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a content-level PII classification scanner for files exposed through an S3 Access Point, using Amazon Comprehend's DetectPiiEntities to identify sensitive data and storing the results in a DynamoDB table with optional SNS notifications. By default the scanner Lambda should run outside any VPC, which is the simplest path and only works if the access point being scanned is internet-origin; before invoking, the access point's NetworkOrigin should be checked (via the access point's describe/get call) and if it comes back as VPC-scoped, the VPC ID, subnet IDs, a security group ID, and route table IDs must be supplied so the Lambda can be deployed inside that same VPC to reach it, since these all default to empty for the outside-VPC case. When a VPC ID is supplied, the template should optionally create the VPC endpoints needed for the Lambda to reach S3, DynamoDB, Comprehend, and SNS, controlled by a create-endpoints flag that defaults to true; this flag should be set to false instead if the target VPC already has any of those four endpoints, since a duplicate Interface endpoint for a service that already has one, or a second S3 Gateway endpoint bound to the same route tables, will fail and roll back the whole stack. The template should include a DynamoDB table for classification reports with point-in-time recovery and encryption, an IAM role granting the Lambda permissions to read from the access point, call Comprehend, write to DynamoDB, publish to SNS, and create logs, and a Lambda function with configurable memory (defaulting to 512 MB), timeout (defaulting to 600 seconds), a default Comprehend language code (defaulting to English, i.e. 'en'), and a default maximum number of files to scan per invocation (defaulting to 500, as a cost and runtime control). The Lambda code should handle chunking of large files, sampling, and pagination through the access point's objects. The stack should output the scanner function ARN, the report table name, and an example CLI invocation command.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates the IAM roles, instance profiles, and managed policies required for Cluster API Provider AWS (CAPA) to manage Kubernetes clusters on AWS, including support for EKS. The template should define roles for the control plane, nodes, and controllers, each named using the prefixes "control-plane.", "nodes.", and "controllers." combined with the suffix "cluster-api-provider-aws.sigs.k8s.io" (for example "control-plane.cluster-api-provider-aws.sigs.k8s.io"), with corresponding instance profiles following the same naming convention. Additionally, it must include EKS-specific roles for the control plane, node groups, and Fargate, along with the controllers-eks managed policy that grants permissions for EKS cluster management, SSM parameter access, and KMS key operations. All policies should be scoped to the necessary AWS services (EC2, ELB, Auto Scaling, EKS, IAM, Secrets Manager, etc.) and follow the principle of least privilege, including restricting Secrets Manager access to secrets under the "aws.cluster.x-k8s.io/*" path, while allowing CAPA to fully manage the lifecycle of Kubernetes clusters and their underlying infrastructure.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS App Runner service for testing purposes, using the public ECR image "public.ecr.aws/aws-containers/hello-app-runner:latest" and exposing it on port 8000. The service should be named "hello-app-runner" by default, and we need the endpoint URL as an output. Auto-deployments should be disabled for this test service.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a CodeBuild project to automatically build and deploy the cfn-postgresql-user-provider Lambda function across all AWS regions whenever a new git tag is pushed to the binxio/cfn-postgresql-user-provider GitHub repository. The project should use the amazonlinux2-x86_64-standard:4.0 build image with privileged mode enabled, run the deploy-all-regions make target, and store the built Lambda artifacts in S3 buckets prefixed with "binxio-public". The build should be triggered via a webhook on tag pushes, and the CodeBuild logs should be retained for 7 days.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure ElastiCache Redis infrastructure for storing session data, using the stack prefix "sera" and importing existing subnet IDs, a KMS key ARN and ID, and a security group ID from the same stack. The template should set up a Redis 7.1 replication group with two cache nodes using cache.m6g.large instances, enable Multi-AZ and automatic failover, enforce transit and at-rest encryption, and use a custom port of 19703. It must also create a subnet group from three imported subnets, a Secrets Manager secret for a Redis AUTH token (generated with a 32-character password excluding special characters) encrypted with the imported KMS key, a disabled default user for migration compatibility using that password, an IAM-based user for modern authentication, and a user group containing both users. The template should export the Redis endpoint, port, replication group ID and ARN, the IAM user ARN and name, and the AUTH token secret ARN for cross-stack references.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of four CodeBuild projects for testing purposes, all using the same imported service role and building from an S3 source bucket with the key "codebuild-demo-test/0123ab9a371ebf0187b0fe5614fbb72c". Each project should use a Linux container with the smallest compute type and the standard 5.0 image, and they should not produce artifacts. The projects should be tagged with a "Project" key of "BadCodeBuildExample" and include a "ProjectPart" tag with the stack name and a "ProjectPartDetail" tag with the project name. The first project should have no logging configuration, the second should enable CloudWatch logs but not specify a log group, the third should specify a hardcoded log group name "log_group_name", and the fourth should reference a CloudWatch log group resource that is created as part of the stack. The log group resource should be set to delete when the stack is deleted or updated.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of Amazon Athena named queries for analyzing AppStream 2.0 usage data from an existing database named "appstream-usage", providing pre-built queries for current and previous month comparisons of average session length per stack, daily session counts, all session details, streaming hours per user, and unique users per application, all aimed at simplifying monthly reporting and analysis of AppStream 2.0 session metrics.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates EventBridge rules in our account to forward critical operational events to a central monitoring account (578003269847) in us-east-2, each rule targeting a specific organization-level event bus by name and assuming a corresponding pre-existing IAM role for delivery: CloudWatch alarm state changes go to the CloudWatch-org-sink bus via role PRX-CloudWatchOrgSinkRole, CloudFormation resource, stack, and stack set status changes (covering the Resource Status Change, Stack Status Change, StackSet Status Change, and StackSet Operation Status Change detail-types) go to the CloudFormation-org-sink bus via role PRX-CloudFormationOrgSinkRole, GuardDuty findings go to the GuardDuty-org-sink bus via role PRX-GuardDutyOrgSinkRole, Slack message relay payloads go to the Slack-org-sink bus via role PRX-SlackOrgSinkRole, and AutoScaling lifecycle and instance refresh events go to the AutoScaling-org-sink bus via role PRX-AutoScalingOrgSinkRole, matching the EC2 Instance Launch Successful, EC2 Instance Launch Unsuccessful, EC2 Instance Terminate Successful, and EC2 Instance Terminate Unsuccessful detail-types plus the EC2 Auto Scaling Instance Refresh Checkpoint Reached, Started, Succeeded, Failed, and Cancelled detail-types.
